Squirrels collecting nuts in autumn might take different routes due to food availability and seasonal changes in their natural habitat.
Factors such as food sources, predators, weather conditions, or human disturbances cannot be fully understood within a laboratory.
While computer simulations can help forecast behavior patterns, they may not be able to explain why these changes occur to the full extent.
Advances in computer technology have made it easier to simulate complex biological systems in animals' natural habitat.
To gain a real understanding of animal behavior, observing them in their natural environment is necessary, which can only be accomplished through field studies.
